clues.name: The Stopped Clock

closeup.title: The Grandfather Clock
closeup.caption: It has not been wound since. The storm did this, not the household.

clues.note: The hall clock stopped at 10:47 and never restarted while I watched. The storm cut the power at that moment -- my first fixed point of the night.
clues.toast: The Stopped Clock -- 10:47, when the power died.

clues.name: The Dry Umbrella

closeup.title: The Umbrella Stand
closeup.caption: It rained all night. Nothing here got wet after ten.

clues.note: One umbrella, Julian Ashcombe's by its tag, dry as a bone. Whatever rain the stand has seen, it saw it before ten-fifteen.
clues.toast: The Dry Umbrella -- nobody came by the front door after ten.

clues.name: The Coat Pegs

closeup.title: Three Coats and an Empty Peg
closeup.caption: Peggy's mac, Tobias's oilskin, Edmund's raincoat. The fourth peg holds only dust.

clues.note: Three coats: Peggy's mac, Tobias's oilskin, Edmund's raincoat. No doctor's coat, no second umbrella. If Dr. Marsh came to this house, she came by another door.
clues.toast: The Coat Pegs -- no doctor's coat or umbrella in the house.

clues.name: Prints on the Mat

closeup.title: The Door Mat
closeup.caption: One pair of brogues, walking in, drying at the edges.

clues.note: One tidy pair of brogue prints walking in, drying at the edges, then trampled by the morning's feet. Only one visitor used the front door -- and some time ago.
clues.toast: Prints on the Mat -- one visitor, some time ago.

clues.name: The House Ledger

closeup.title: Colette's Ledger
closeup.caption: The most honest witness in the house keeps her own book.

clues.note: Colette's ledger: 'Sat -- Mr. A. at nine, gone quarter past ten.' The front door's whole story of the night, in her hand.
clues.toast: The House Ledger -- Julian in at nine, gone a quarter past ten.

clues.name: The Sealed Letter

closeup.title: In the Mail Tray
closeup.caption: Addressed and sealed, waiting for the Monday post that never carried it.

clues.note: Sealed for the morning post: 'new instructions for my will -- come Tuesday. E.V.' Whatever he meant to change, he never posted it.
clues.toast: The Sealed Letter -- 'new instructions for my will'.

clues.name: A Horn Button

closeup.title: On the Stair Carpet
closeup.caption: Small, old, and probably nothing at all.

clues.note: A horn button off someone's coat, on the stair carpet. Small, old, and probably nothing at all -- but the notebook keeps it anyway.
clues.toast: A Horn Button -- a small thing, kept.

clues.name: The Confession Manuscript

closeup.title: A Confession of Sorts
closeup.caption: Pages forty to forty-three, gone from the binding.

clues.note: 'A Confession of Sorts.' The preface is whiskey-stained and two whole signatures -- pages forty to forty-three -- are torn from the binding. Something was tucked at page thirty-nine.
clues.toast: The Confession -- pages 40 to 43 torn out.

clues.name: A Torn Slip

closeup.title: Torn Slip, Page 39
closeup.caption: 'for H.M. -- before Monday. E.V.'

clues.note: 'for H.M. -- before Monday. E.V.' He was sending pages to someone with those initials, and soon. H.M. who never came, or came quietly.
clues.toast: A Torn Slip -- 'for H.M. -- before Monday'.

clues.name: Edmund Vesper

closeup.title: The Wing Chair
closeup.caption: He died reading. The page wears his whiskey; the table keeps his spectacles.

clues.note: He died reading: spectacles folded on the page, spine settled into the wing chair, one slipper off. No wound, no struggle. Whatever took him was already inside him -- and there is more on the side table than spectacles.
clues.toast: Edmund Vesper -- dead reading, no wound, no struggle.

clues.name: His Heart Drops

closeup.title: Tincture of Digitalis
closeup.caption: Dr. H. Marsh's label, five drops in water, half used.

clues.note: His ordinary heart drops, Dr. H. Marsh's label, half used. If he had overdosed from his own bottle the timing would not fit -- and the bottle is nearly neat. The wrong bottle, the right name.
clues.toast: His Heart Drops -- the label names Dr. H. Marsh.

clues.name: The Nightcap Glass

closeup.title: The Tumbler
closeup.caption: Two-thirds drunk -- and a film above the liquor line.

clues.note: His nightcap, two-thirds drunk. Above the liquor line, inside the glass, a dull film -- like a varnish ring. Whatever made that film was carried in the drink itself.
clues.toast: The Nightcap Glass -- a dull film above the liquor line.

clues.name: The Whiskey Decanter

closeup.title: The Decanter
closeup.caption: Dosed before he poured. The stopper sits quiet on it still.

clues.note: Film on the inner shoulder above the waterline, the same dull varnish as the glass. The decanter was dosed -- not his glass. The poison waited, patient, for his nightly pour.
clues.toast: The Decanter -- dosed before he poured.

clues.name: Ash at the Ember Edge

closeup.title: What the Fire Missed
closeup.caption: Purple petals and a leaf midrib -- foxglove, burned in a hurry.

clues.note: Through the glass: a crushed leaf midrib, and two purple petals the fire missed. Foxglove. Someone burned the evidence in the ember edge, and the hearth kept a little of it.
clues.toast: Ash at the Ember Edge -- foxglove petals, burned.

clues.name: The Fallen Mantel Clock

closeup.title: Face-in, 11:38
closeup.caption: It stopped when it fell; he staggered when it fell.

clues.note: The mantel clock fell face-in and stopped at 11:38. He staggered at 11:38 -- and whatever was inside him had been working for some minutes before that.
clues.toast: The Mantel Clock -- down at 11:38, my second fixed point.

clues.name: A Ghost of a Print

closeup.title: Diamond-Tread, Rain-Damp
closeup.caption: Size seven or eight -- and none of the household's boots.

clues.note: A diamond-tread boot print ghosting the rug by the fender -- rain-damp, size seven or eight. None of the household wears treads like that. The garden, then.
clues.toast: A Ghost of a Print -- diamond tread, size seven or eight.

clues.name: Sewing Scissors

closeup.title: On the Sideboard
closeup.caption: Ten paces from the door she says she never left.

clues.note: Peggy's sewing scissors, ten paces from the door she says she never left. She was in this room after ten -- whatever her story is worth.
clues.toast: Sewing Scissors -- Peggy was here after ten.

clues.name: The Garden Door Bolt

closeup.title: Left Off the Bolt
closeup.caption: Fresh scratches bright on the latch plate; the bolt never thrown.

clues.note: The kitchen-garden door: bolt left off, fresh scratches bright on the latch plate. Someone came and went by the garden while the household sat in the dark.
clues.toast: The Garden Door -- bolt left off, scratches bright.

clues.name: Colette's Round

closeup.title: Her Midnight Patrol
closeup.caption: Found off the bolt at half eleven; bolted on the spot.

clues.note: Colette, fetching the milk at half eleven: the garden door stood off its bolt, and she bolted it. The scratches were bright. In thirty-one years she has never once left it so -- so the door was used in the dark, and more than once.
clues.toast: Colette's Round -- the door found off the bolt at half eleven.

clues.name: The Clatter From Above

closeup.title: Two Floors Up
closeup.caption: A clatter like a clock falling -- then quiet.

clues.note: Tobias, inking in the attic: 'a clatter like a clock falling, a few minutes after half eleven -- then quiet.' The quiet, he says, was worse. The mantel clock fell at 11:38; his ears fix the death within minutes of it.
clues.toast: The Clatter -- heard some minutes after half eleven.

clues.name: Peggy's Own Admission

closeup.title: Twenty to Eleven
closeup.caption: Her uncle alive and humming, a folder under his arm.

clues.note: Peggy says it plainly: she came down at twenty to eleven for her scissors, found her uncle crossing the hall humming with a folder of pages under his arm, and went back up to sew. Alive, cheerful, carrying the memoir -- at twenty to eleven.
clues.toast: Peggy's Admission -- her uncle alive and humming at twenty to eleven.

clues.name: The Burnt Loaf

closeup.title: Under a Blackened Crust
closeup.caption: Burnt past saving -- not stopped half-baked.

clues.note: The morning's loaf went in at 10:35 and the blackout killed the oven at 10:47. If the power had stayed off, the loaf would sit there half-baked. It is burnt black past saving: the oven came back at 11:21 and finished its work to cinders while Colette was elsewhere. The kitchen kept its own timetable of the dark.
clues.toast: The Burnt Loaf -- burnt, not raw: the oven came back without her.

clues.name: The Pantry Lantern

closeup.title: One Flame Through the Dark
closeup.caption: Oil burned to the wick's mark -- half an hour of one small light.

clues.note: Colette's hurricane lantern, hung back on its pantry hook with the oil burned down and a soot halo on the shelf. It lit one corner of one kitchen through the dark half hour -- and it was the only moving light downstairs. Whoever used the garden door crossed the house without a flame, and without one on the way out.
clues.toast: The Pantry Lantern -- one moving light downstairs, and it was hers.

clues.name: The Wireless, Still On

closeup.title: Singing to Nobody
closeup.caption: Left switched on since the lights came back.

clues.note: The kitchen wireless died mid-song at 10:47 with everything else -- and this morning it is playing again, switched on all night. Nobody turned it back on: the power returned at 11:21 and found the kitchen empty. Colette was out on her rounds, the bread burning behind her, and the wireless sang to nobody while a door stood off its bolt.
clues.toast: The Wireless -- singing to an empty kitchen at 11:21.

clues.name: Wet Prints on the Flags

closeup.title: Diamond-Tread, Crossing In
closeup.caption: Rain-wet, walking in from the garden door -- and out again.

clues.note: Stone flags keep a wet story longer than a rug does: diamond-tread prints, rain-damp, size seven or eight, walking in from the garden door and out again -- toward the passage, the hall, the parlour. The same boots that ghosted the rug by the fender. Rain-wet, so they fell while the storm still beat: inside the dark half hour.
clues.toast: Wet Prints on the Flags -- the garden visitor crossed the kitchen twice.

clues.name: The Kitchen Rounds Book

closeup.title: Her Rounds, in Pencil
closeup.caption: 10:35 bread in. 11:21 lights back, kitchen empty. 11:30 the door, off its bolt.

clues.note: A second book by the flour bin, pencil in a tidy hand: '10:35 -- bread in, wireless on. 10:47 -- dark; lantern lit. 11:21 -- lights back, wireless singing; I was in the scullery. 11:30 -- garden door OFF its bolt; bolted it. Never left it so.' The most honest witness in the house has said it all before -- and now she has written it too.
clues.toast: The Rounds Book -- 10:35 to half eleven, in her own hand.

clues.name: The Worn Runner

closeup.title: Lanes Worn by Habit
closeup.caption: Two pale lanes, a stick's dark line -- and fresh wax on the twelfth step.

clues.note: Years of the same feet wear lanes into a stair carpet: Edmund's stick along the right, Colette's trays close against the wall, and the middle left for whoever else goes up. On the twelfth step, three fresh wax drips -- candle wax, carried DOWN, the way Tobias banks his light at midnight. Habit, written in carpet: last night everyone's road was the road they always take.
clues.toast: The Worn Runner -- habit's lanes, and a midnight candle's wax.

clues.name: The Tonic Glass

closeup.title: Rinsed, and Left Upside Down
closeup.caption: The doctor's tonic -- iron and quinine, one dose gone.

clues.note: On the sill shelf outside Peggy's door: Dr. Marsh's tonic bottle -- iron and quinine, harmless, nearly full -- and a glass rinsed and left upside down to dry. She took her nightly tonic standing on the landing, at her leisure, then went in to sew. A woman settling for the night, not one dressing to go out.
clues.toast: The Tonic Glass -- Peggy settled for the night, unhurried.

clues.name: The Candle's Mark

closeup.title: Burned to the Eleven Mark
closeup.caption: A wax ridge exactly where an eleven-o'clock flame died.

clues.note: Her bedside candle burned down to a ridge of wax that stops at the eleven-o'clock mark: she lit it when the dark came and blew it out when she slept, at eleven or just after. A woman asleep at eleven does not hear a clock wound at midnight -- and no winding happened anyway. The hall clock stood dead from 10:47.
clues.toast: The Candle's Mark -- burned to eleven; then sleep.

clues.name: The Final Notice

closeup.title: In the Writing Case
closeup.caption: Red-stamped paper: FINAL. And IOUs in a neat pile.

clues.note: A final notice from the Meridian Credit & Loan, stamped across the day's post, and a packet of IOUs in her own hand. Drowning, and expecting the house to save her -- until Tuesday's letter, which is about a trust, not money. Debts make want; Tuesday made her frightened; neither made her a murderer.
clues.toast: The Final Notice -- Peggy's debts are her own, and they are not the murder.

clues.name: The Journal by the Bed

closeup.title: His Private Book
closeup.caption: 'R. drew the fox first. The safe keeps her pages.'

clues.note: A leather journal in careful pencil: 'Ruth drew the fox before I did. Her books are mine to keep until the preface says so out loud. The safe keeps her pages -- the little key hangs on the ribbon, where a fox sleeps.' The key is on the ribbon still. Edmund's room keeps his past folded, and the past has a name: Ruth Marsh.
clues.toast: The Journal -- Ruth Marsh, and a safe that keeps her pages.

clues.name: The Medicine Cabinet

closeup.title: Everything in Its Place
closeup.caption: Three shelves, one hand. The doctor labels what she leaves.

clues.note: Iron and quinine for Peggy, aspirin for the household, and Edmund's digitalis -- a fresh refill, nearly full, in Dr. Marsh's neat print: 'five drops in water'. She restocks this cabinet monthly; the receipt book says so. Everything here is ordinary, and everything here is hers. The right name again -- in the wrong bottle.
clues.toast: The Medicine Cabinet -- the doctor restocks the house's medicines.

clues.name: The Blotter's Impression

closeup.title: Under the Torch
closeup.caption: Pencil pressure keeps what blotting-paper hides.

clues.note: The desk blotter, under the torch: a pencil plea pressed deep by a shaking hand. 'I never meant -- the memoir -- let me make it right by Christmas, only don't go to the societies. J.A.' Julian Ashcombe leaned on this desk at ten past ten and begged. His 'I never heard of any memoir' dies here, in his own graphite.
clues.toast: The Blotter -- Julian's plea, pressed in pencil.

clues.name: A Cab Receipt

closeup.title: Dropped in the Basket
closeup.caption: The Bell & Curtain rank. 10:19 p.m. Hall Lane.

clues.note: A cab receipt, crumpled in the waste basket: 'The Bell & Curtain rank -- 10:19 p.m. -- Hall Lane.' Julian left the house at a quarter past ten and was in a cab four minutes later, gone before the storm's first lightning. Whatever his guilt about sketches, his feet were elsewhere by the dark half hour.
clues.toast: The Cab Receipt -- Julian in a cab at 10:19, gone from the story.

clues.name: The Safe's Carbons

closeup.title: Pages 40 to 43
closeup.caption: Carbon copies -- the fire never saw these.

clues.note: Inside the little wall safe, a folder of carbon copies: pages forty to forty-three of 'A Confession of Sorts', Edmund's careful hand doubling through the sheet. 'Ruth Marsh drew the Hollow fox before I ever did. I mean to say so in print, her name on every line, while I live to sign the preface.' He kept carbons of everything; the originals were torn from the binding and left the house in the dark half hour -- and only one person carried pages out that night.
clues.toast: The Safe's Carbons -- pp. 40-43 survive; the originals left the house.

clues.name: The Apprentice's Tin

closeup.title: Buttons and Needles
closeup.caption: Two horn buttons, spare, off the same card.

clues.note: On the study's work shelf, Tobias's tin: needles, wax, thread, and two horn buttons still on their card -- the same cast as the one on the stair carpet. Lost days ago on his attic climb, swept along by the morning brooms. The button was never a stranger's; it was the house mending itself.
clues.toast: The Apprentice's Tin -- the stair button's spare, found.
